notes: With-skill 36/36 vs baseline 27/36, single run per configuration, so treat the gap as directional.

Three baseline failures are template compliance only the skill knows (work record, correction entry, deal-specific marker); three more are borderline wording calls. The clearest substantive baseline failures: it decided for the human ('Don't sign with Day 60', prescribed a counter on the haircut) and never referred contract rights to counsel.
Two cases do not discriminate (first-time buyer, ten lenders): baseline passes everything.

With-skill responses are 1.5-2x longer; most of the extra is fixed scaffolding (header, status labels, self-check, work record). Pencil-correction response is 1,573 words and repeats the 6.70% -> 6.22% change four times.
INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE status appears in 6 of 7 with-skill runs: accurate, but reads as boilerplate when no documents were supplied.
Baseline invented inputs to reach verdicts (debt terms, a Day 100-105 estimate, a $1.2M anchor, a per-foot price in the owner script); with-skill did not. No assertion currently measures this.
Haircut case is contaminated in the skill's favor: the skill's worked sample uses the same prompt.
